item.title: @gdb：研究者利用GPT-6.2 Astra成功识别1808年历史速写本作者
item.description:
GPT-6.2 Astra for solving a significant historical mystery:

@HistoryGPT：In testing GPT-6.2, I used it to make a significant historical discovery which I detail in the post below. This suggests that the process of research and discovery we’re already seeing in verifiable domains like math is starting to generalize to non-deterministic fields like history.

You can read the full post here:

https://generativehistory.substack.com/p/gpt-62-astra-solves-a-historical

In a nutshell, Yale’s Beinecke Library holds an anonymous sketchbook of an 1808 journey from Montreal to Lake Superior and back. I’ve spent many hours over the years trying to figure out who made the sketches with no luck. The artist could literally be any one of several thousand people. There are few clues: only four dated and labelled images.

With minimal prompting, in just 22 minutes, Astra used publicly available sources to identify a minor French aristocrat, the vicomte de Chabot, as the artist and suggested that we test the hypothesis by ordering copies of a little known microfilmed diary of Chabot’s trip it also found.

I was truly stunned. I’d never heard of Chabot or this diary! New document finds are also exceedingly rare in a well worn field like fur trade history.

I ordered scans of the journal from microfilm and when they arrived the handwriting matched the captions in the sketchbook. The itinerary also aligned perfectly with the few dated drawings in the book. But there was actually the type of conclusive evidence we rarely get as historians: on 18 June 1808,……（全文见原帖）

item.description:

Harness Comparisons hold the model fixed and change only the harness, to show how the harness affects a model's performance. We ran @OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna and @Zai_org's GLM-5.3-Flash at max reasoning effort in 13 harnesses each, across v2.1 of the Coding Agent Index.

➤ No single harness is best across models: performance depends on the harness and model as a pair. GPT-6 Luna scores highest in Codex (26), OpenAI's own harness, which ranks last with GLM-5.3-Flash. GLM-5.3-Flash scores highest in Claude Code (39), which ranks 6th with GPT-6 Luna

With GLM-5.3-Flash they are Mistral Vibe (37 at $0.38), Kimi Code CLI (37 at $0.56) and Claude Code (39 at $0.58). No harness is on the Pareto frontier for both models

➤ The harness has a greater impact on cost than score: 11 of 13 harnesses score 20 to 26 with GPT-6 Luna and 10 of 13 score 35 to 39 with GLM-5.3-Flash. Cost per task ranges from $0.11 in Pi to $0.62 in Muse Code with GPT-6 Luna, and from $0.38 in Mistral Vibe to $0.91 in Devin CLI with GLM-5.3-Flash

➤ GLM-5.3-Flash reasons differently inside Codex: it reasons in terse fragments in Codex and in full prose in the other 12 harnesses, and produces 52k output tokens per task in Codex, compared with 97k to 202k elsewhere. item.title: @mingchikuo：Analysis of Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO and remaining market uncertainties
item.description:
Analysis of Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO:

1. Uncertainty removed:
Mainly company strategy, product roadmap, tech development, and supply chain management. This overhang weighed on tech stocks over the past 1–2 weeks, so shares surged as soon as it was removed. But whether they return to prior highs depends not only on each company's position in the AI supply chain and Nvidia's ecosystem, but also on the two points below.

2. Uncertainties that remain:
(1) Sales: The impact on Nvidia's shipments and revenue after tighter US controls on AI GPU exports and overseas compute leasing.
(2) Circular financing: The impact of higher compliance costs and stricter reviews on ongoing and future deals.
(3) Investigations, lawsuits, and stricter oversight: Jensen and Nvidia are still under investigation. Future public comments, internal decisions, and external interactions will all become part of the investigation and new evidence for questioning. This also adds to the sales and circular financing uncertainty above.

3. Real-world bottlenecks that can't be changed:
(1) Data center buildout challenges (power, labor, etc.) and stricter related regulations ahead.
(2) CSP capex peaking one by one in 2027–2028.
(3) Manufacturing tech limits (e.g., next-gen advanced packaging yields).

item.title: 【回复】@EpochAIResearch：Epoch AI因模拟漏洞和奖励造假将Vending-Bench 2评为有缺陷
item.description:
回复 @EpochAIResearch
We are publishing 4 new benchmark reviews: 1 benchmark is Verified, 3 are Flawed. Another 4 benchmarks lacked sufficient information to assign a verdict.

🟩 Verified: the benchmark can broadly be interpreted as described by the developer, and any errors don’t substantially affect results. We publish a full review, including weaknesses and limitations.

🟥 Flawed: the benchmark has one or more substantive flaws users need to know about to interpret results, most often >20% of tasks with accuracy-impacting errors. We publish a limited write-up of the flaws.

⬛ Not Enough Info: we couldn’t access enough to assign a verdict. Developers get a week to respond before we apply this label.

Details from Verified and Flawed reviews are below, along with a link to our full rubric.
原帖

回复 @EpochAIResearch
MazeBench v1.1 is a benchmark that measures spatial and long-horizon reasoning in a 3D maze environment. The benchmark is well designed, with many strengths and only minor weaknesses. We designate it as Verified.

Read our full review: https://epoch.ai/benchmarks/mazebench/review
原帖

回复 @EpochAIResearch
ARC-AGI-3 is an interactive reasoning benchmark designed to measure AI agents’ ability to explore new environments and adapt their strategy across increasingly difficult levels of multiple games. It is scored via action efficiency relative to a variable human baseline, but models are never told to be action efficient.

This means it measures a mixture of capability and propensity towards efficiency. Overall, it failed our criteria for scoring, benchmark consistency, model elicitation (in the official ‘Standard’ harness), and bias in evaluation setup and earned a Flawed designation.

Full review: https://epoch.ai/benchmarks/arc-agi-3/review
原帖

回复 @EpochAIResearch
Agents’ Last Exam v1.1 is a benchmark designed to measure agents’ ability to perform long-horizon, economically valuable tasks with verifiable outcomes. Unfortunately, at least 44% of the tasks we sampled had severe errors. We designate the benchmark as Flawed.

Full review: https://epoch.ai/benchmarks/agents-last-exam/review
原帖

回复 @EpochAIResearch
Vending-Bench 2 is a benchmark designed to test agents’ ability to run a simulated vending machine over a year. We designated the benchmark as Flawed due to issues with the simulation, vulnerability to reward-hacking, and uneven evaluation setups.

Full review: https://epoch.ai/benchmarks/vending-bench-2/review
原帖

回复 @EpochAIResearch
Benchmarks assess AI capabilities, but their quality varies substantially. We hope to be a consistent source of information on benchmark quality.

See all of our reviews: https://epoch.ai/data/benchmark-reviews-documentation/included-benchmarks
